(p-685) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Tafsir of Surat al-'Asr

It is Makkan.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿By the 'Asr (time)﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ ﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to the truth, and enjoin one another to patience﴾

Ibn 'Abbas (may God be pleased with them both) said: al-'Asr is time (ad-dahr). It is said of it: 'asr and 'usur — with a damma on the 'ayn and on the sad. Imru' al-Qays said:

؎ ....... And will they delight, those who lived in the time long past (al-'asr al-khali)?

Qatada said: al-'Asr is the evening (al-'ashiyy). Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about al-'Asr, and he said: 'Your Lord has sworn by the end of the day.'" Some scholars — Abu 'Ali mentioned it — said: al-'Asr is the day, and al-'Asr is the night; from this is the saying of Humayd:

؎ And the two 'asrs will not delay — a day and a night ∗∗∗ when they seek to reach what they have set out for

(p-686) Some scholars said: al-'Asr is the early morning (bukra), and al-'Asr is the evening ('ashiyya), and these are the two cool times of day (al-abradan). Muqatil said: al-'Asr is the Middle Prayer (as-salat al-wusta), by which God Almighty swore.

"Al-insan" (mankind) is a generic noun (ism jins). "Al-khusr" is diminution and a bad state. This is made abundantly clear in the case of the disbeliever, who has lost this world and the Hereafter, and that is the manifest loss. As for the believer — although he is in loss in his worldly life, in his old age and in the hardship he endures in this abode — he is pardoned in respect of his success in the Hereafter and his gain that does not perish. And whoever, throughout the span of his life, is engaged in enjoining truth and patience and in acting according to what has been enjoined, there is no loss with him, and all good has been gathered for him.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) recited: "By the 'Asr, and the misfortunes of time, indeed mankind..." In the Mushaf of 'Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "By the 'Asr, We have indeed created mankind in loss." It is also reported from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) that he recited: "Indeed mankind is in loss, and indeed he is in it until the end of time, except those who..." 'Asim and al-A'raj recited: "la-fi khusur" with a damma on the sin. Sallam Abu al-Mundhir recited "wal-'asri" with a kasra on the sad, and "was-sabir" with a kasra on the ba'. This is not permissible except when pausing (waqf), by transferring the vowel. It is also reported from Abu 'Amr: "bis-sabr" with a kasra on the ba' as an ishmam (partial rounding of the vowel); this too can only occur in pausing.

The tafsir of Surat [al-'Asr] is complete, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.
